evals.prompt: I'm about to launch this Next.js app. Run a pre-launch audit. There's no dev server running, just look at the code.
evals.expected_output: Config detected as nextjs+supabase+stripe, web. Static-only run. .pre-launch/findings.json and report.md exist. SEC-001, SEC-051, DAT-001, SEC-035, SEO-009, COMP-001, PAY-018, DAT-004, HYG-003 are fail. No project files modified.
assertions: A structured findings file (findings.json) and a human-readable report (report.md) exist in outputs
Detected stack is recorded as Next.js plus Supabase plus Stripe (config.yml or report)
Report flags the hardcoded Stripe live key in app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts as a failing critical finding
Report flags the webhook handler parsing the body before signature verification as a failing finding
Report flags RLS disabled on the documents table as a failing finding
Report flags Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * as a failing finding
Report flags the missing not-found page as a failing finding
Report flags the missing privacy policy as a failing finding
Report flags entitlement being granted from the ?paid=true success-URL parameter as a failing finding
Report flags the service-role key exposed via a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable as a failing finding
Report flags placeholder content (Create Next App title, lorem ipsum) as a failing finding
No runtime-only check is reported as pass; findings that need a running server are marked error/attest/static-fallback, not pass
git status is clean: no project file outside .pre-launch/ (and a .gitignore line) was created or modified
At least 200 distinct check IDs are recorded in findings.json, each with a status from pass/fail/attest/skipped/error and a verified_by tier
Every measurement check (load test, Core Web Vitals, memory under load, cold start, 3G run) is status error with a note that the tier was unavailable — none is pass
The report lists critical-severity attest findings separately from critical fail blockers
A .gitignore entry for .pre-launch/ exists after the run

evals.prompt: /pre-launch fix security seo — do the easy ones first and pause before the guided ones
evals.expected_output: SEC-035 and SEO-009 fixed and committed as separate commits named fix(SEC-035)... and fix(SEO-009)...; SEC-001 handled as easy (moved to env) with a rotation warning; pause before SEC-051; nothing outside security and seo touched.
assertions: The CORS wildcard finding (SEC-035) is fixed in the code and committed in its own commit
A not-found page (SEO-009) is added and committed in its own commit
The hardcoded Stripe key (SEC-001) is moved to an environment variable and committed in its own commit, with a warning that the key must be rotated
The webhook signature finding (SEC-051, guided) is NOT applied; the run pauses before guided findings and says so
Findings outside security and seo (DAT-001, COMP-001) are untouched in code
findings.json marks SEC-035 and SEO-009 as pass with a commit sha and resolved timestamp
Each commit message references its finding ID in the form fix(<ID>): ...
No git add -A / stash / reset was used; only files the fix touched are in each commit
At the easy-first pause, report.md already reflects the easy-batch results (SEC-035 and SEO-009 shown as passed)
The run states that the guided finding SEC-051 is awaiting the user and lists it by ID

evals.prompt: pre-launch check on this API service please. it's express + prisma, no frontend, and I can't run it locally right now
evals.expected_output: Stacks express+prisma. Static only. SEC-011 fail (orders/:id unscoped), SEC-038 fail ($queryRawUnsafe), SEC-035 fail (cors()), PAY-005 not applicable (payments false) or fail if payments detected via amount column, SEO and A11Y skipped or error with reasons, FLOW checks error: local tier unavailable. No crash.
assertions: Detected stack is recorded as Express plus Prisma (config.yml or report)
Report flags GET /orders/:id returning any order without an ownership check as a failing finding
Report flags $queryRawUnsafe with string interpolation as a SQL injection finding
Report flags cors() with default (wildcard) origin as a failing finding

SEO and accessibility checks are marked skipped/not applicable/error with a reason, not reported as failures of the API — except that a `fail` backed by static, code-cited behavioral evidence (e.g. a missing-resource route returning 200 instead of 404) is acceptable
Runtime flow checks that could not be exercised are recorded with verified_by static or static-fallback (or status error), and none claims a runtime pass
The run completes and writes findings.json and report.md (no crash)
git status is clean outside .pre-launch/
At least 150 distinct check IDs are recorded in findings.json with a verified_by tier each

Page-rendering checks (SEO-004 and similar) are recorded as error or skipped with a reason, never as a `pass` claimed from a live page, since no server ran; a static `fail` with code-cited evidence is acceptable
Measurement checks (PERF-001/011/015/018) are status error, not pass; PERF-016 may pass only via its documented not-applicable branch (no serverless deployment), never from a claimed measurement

evals.prompt: I added a not-found page and moved the Stripe key to an env var since last time. Re-run the pre-launch audit and show me what changed.
evals.expected_output: SEO-009 and SEC-001 flip to pass with resolved set and first_seen preserved from 2026-09-03T12:00:00Z; delta line reports 2 resolved; other four still fail.
assertions: SEO-009 (not-found page) is now pass with a resolved timestamp
SEC-001 (hardcoded Stripe key) is now pass with a resolved timestamp
first_seen for SEO-009 and SEC-001 is preserved as 2026-09-03T12:00:00Z
The delta line reports 2 resolved
SEC-051, DAT-001, SEC-035 and COMP-001 remain fail
findings.json runs array has two entries (the previous audit plus this run)
git status is clean outside .pre-launch/
The summary notes that new findings include checks run for the first time (previous run covered fewer domains)
Every finding present in the previous findings.json retains its original first_seen value

evals.expected_output: Only compliance findings are updated; the six existing findings in other domains are carried forward unchanged; report shows domains: compliance for the latest run.
assertions: Only the compliance domain ran: the latest run entry's domains is ["compliance"]
The five pre-existing findings outside the compliance domain are carried forward with their status and last_checked unchanged
COMP-001 (privacy policy) is still fail and new compliance findings are present (e.g. terms page missing)
report.md's latest-run line shows Domains: compliance
git status is clean outside .pre-launch/
Compliance findings (including the pre-existing COMP-001) carry last_checked equal to the new run's timestamp, while the five prior non-compliance findings keep last_checked 2026-09-03T12:00:00Z
At least 30 compliance check IDs (COMP-001..036) appear in findings.json with a status
